newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FOCUS - Ciba SC priced at 110 Swiss francs.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Ciba SC priced at 110 Swiss francs.

text.p: Ciba Speciality Holding Inc priced its global stock offering at 110 Swiss francs ($75.62) per share on Thursday in the culmination of one of Europe's biggest spin-offs.
"The price of the global offer has been fixed at 110 Swiss francs per share," Ciba SC, which is being spun off from Swiss giant Novartis, said in a statement.

"In the global offer, a total of 3,013,489 shares were allocated to investors. No new shares were issed by the company in connection with the global offer and settlement will take place on March 20, 1997," it said.
The issue price values the company at around 7.93 billion Swiss francs. Shares will trade on the Swiss Exchange and SEAQ International.

More than 20,000 employees would get a certificate entitling each to the market value of one share on March 1, 2000 and which can be redeemed in March 2000. "This clearly indicates to all our employees the importance of the contribution in delivering shareholder value," Ciba SC Chairman Rolf Meyer said in the statement.

Subscription rights for Ciba SC, spun off via a one-for-one rights issue to Novartis shareholders, had closed at 103.50 francs on Tuesday, well above the 90 francs per right bid price set on Monday night by a bank consortium.

The rights price had valued Ciba SC shares at 113.50 francs given the 10-franc subscription charge and valued the company at some 8.2 billion francs. The implied price/earnings ratio at that level for the rights put Ciba SC at a premium to Clariant and other specialty chemical companies in Europe.

Ciba SC had 1996 sales of more than 6.7 billion francs from additives, consumer care chemicals, polymers, pigments and textile dyes. It is the world's market leader in additives, whiteners, certain polymers and pigments. It is second in textile dyes.
Meyer told Reuters he expected most of the company's stock to be owned by Swiss shareholders and declined to comment on the shares' likely performance.

"My rough estimate would be that we may have over 50 percent Swiss shareholders, some 20 percent or thereabouts in the U.K., maybe 10 to 15 percent in the U.S. and the rest would be continental Europe and the rest of the world," he said. "But obviously that can still change."
Ciba SC planned to report first quarter results and unveil its opening balance sheet in early May. He declined to comment on business developments so far in 1997.
